"But every once in a while, things line up in such a way as to make the game... a frustrating grind,"

In the three games we've played so far, Skinwalker.

I noted it in the general discussion thread, but... sheesh. He starts with a 25 HP relic you pretty much have to deal with. Then Skinny typically plays one card per turn and it's probably a minion (21 cards in his deck are a minion) or a card that brings out a minion. Or both. Three of those minions have 25 HPs. The Voodoo Pins have 9 HP each.

Then he plays most likely another few minions as you deal with the environment deck. And lord help us if you play Unity or even Visionary against him. (Oddly, Wagner Base with 3 targets may be the best environment choice against him. Are their E-decks with equal or less minions?)

There's a lot of damage reduction in there for Skinny and his Zombies, and even a bit for his minions in general.

And Skinny has 150 HP on top of all that.

Basically it's a shooting gallery. Pick your optimal targets, sure, but basically just shoot and shoot and shoot. And you're so busy dealing with the Pins and Relics and any other inherent minion annoyance abilities that you rarely have time to shoot Skinny.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
Envisioner:

Plague Rat is another villain I'd like to see adjusted to remove his glaringly obvious weaknesses.  I love how hyper-violent he is, but very early in my time playing the game, I read a game report about him on Mars where Meteor Storm came out, and he couldn't remove it, so the heroes just ignored him while they built up to OHK him after finally removing it.

Meteor Storm does this to a lot of villains, actually - it's the reason I rarely play on Wagner (unless it's against someone like Advanced Blade, or Warlord Voss, who can actually make it a threat).  There are a ton of villains with literally no response to it, up to and including Iron Legacy himself, and if the villain can't remove it, they should always lose, since a villain who can destroy stuff faster than the heroes can play it when damage isn't a factor would always win anyway, since the heroes could never get an engine going while damage was happening, either.  Heck, even villains who can destroy Environment cards almost never do so every turn (yeah, yeah, except Spite), so you're almost certain to get a few free plays in.  There's nothing lamer than a game where an Environment card randomly hands the win to the heroes whenever it shows up.

Kismet is a great villain, and I always enjoy taking her on, but after my first game against her (in Advanced, with Tachyon, Legacy, Bunker, and Absolute Zero) was one of the most intense, satisfying games of Sentinels I ever played - and easily the most fun I've had losing in this game - I am always slightly let down when I face her and the team has a lot of Ongoing removal, so I am not constantly agonizing over whether it's worth it to hit my own people.  Anyone who thinks Kismet is too easy should face her with a team like that.

I am also very saddened that the Legacy mirror match doesn't have more meat.  The trope of a hero having to face down an evil version of himself (herself, in Young Legacy's case) for a reason, and I was really looking forward to an epic clash of the Legacies… but in practice, it doesn't really work.  There is every possibility that Legacy gets out Next Evolution and Lead From The Front, totally neutering what would otherwise be the most brutal villain in the game.  Sure, you only have 3-ish turns to get that combo, so it won't happen every time, but the question of whether you draw into it or not has nothing to do with player skill or planning, so I still am not a fan.  I have similar (though less serious)  issues  with Tempest against Voss - get him Hailstorm and a damage boost from any of a number of other heroes, and Voss' minions quickly cease to be any sort of persistent threat.  Advanced Voss and Genebound Guards keep this from becoming quite as absurd, but it's always sad to me when I want to fight a villain using anyone… except their Nemesis.

Ironic

mm, that's not quite my definition of lame.  For it to gimp a villain completely is sad, but if it hands the heroes the game without quite doing that, then it feels like the Environment sided with the heroes to defeat the villain, and there's a nice story in that.  Mostly what bugs me is just that the flavor of Meteor Storm is wrong…it sounds like it should be the name of a card that deals damage (perhaps replacing the awkwardly named Fire in the Biosphere), and the concept of "nobody can do damage" might be better represented by a card called "Isolation Lockdown" or something, where the heroes and villains are all in different domes of the marsbase with sealed bulkheads between (not that this explains why Absolute Zero can't damage himself, but still).

I am always slightly let down when I face her and the team has a lot of Ongoing removal, so I am not constantly agonizing over whether it's worth it to hit my own people.  Anyone who thinks Kismet is too easy should face her with a team like that.

Yeah, in general I feel like the Ongoing cards and removal therefor are one of the weak links of this otherwise excellent game…too many villains have none at all, making their magic bullets useless, and too many heroes lack such bullets, for when they are vitally necessary.  It makes villains that have lots of Targets feel better-designed, because damage is a mechanic that all decks have in common…it makes you have to work at removing the cards, and some take more work than others.  Ongoings lack that interesting element…if you replaced the simple number progression with some sort of puzzle, like having to match sets of icons in order to destroy them, the game would gain something in terms of depth.  Not sure whether it'd be worth it, of course, just thinking aloud.

I am also very saddened that the Legacy mirror match doesn't have more meat.

I thought of that too, when I was wondering why Legacy wasn't one of Evil Paul's nemeses…presumably Iron Legs can't quite bring himself to be quite as brutal with his own naive, younger self as with the naive, younger selves of those who would battle him in the future.  I feel that if there was a confrontation between the IL and any of the heroic Ls, it wouldn't be a battle so much as a war of words, which unfortunately doesn't tend to model well in game form.

There is every possibility that Legacy gets out Next Evolution and Lead From The Front, totally neutering what would otherwise be the most brutal villain in the game.

I have similar (though less serious) issues with Tempest against Voss - get him Hailstorm and a damage boost from any of a number of other heroes, and Voss' minions quickly cease to be any sort of persistent threat.

Except against the Gene-Bound Guards, of course.

Gloomweaver is the Rotting God; his self-damage represents his body of crumbling, necrotic flesh literally falling apart, because his energy of death and decay is destroying everything nearby including his own anchor to the material world.  In order to remain incarnate, he must kill other things in order to harvest their life essences.  ("The only way you can survive is to spread…")  If the heroes lose, Gloomy can swallow their souls and presumably gain enough energy from it to survive the trip to the nearest center of civilization, whereup on he can feed to his heart's content.  You can think of the damage they deal to him as representing a plan to lure him away from potential sources of sustenance.

In the three games we've played so far, Skinwalker.



Just took him on for the first time last night, and it was a lot of fun.  Tempest, Scholar, and Omnitron-X in Megalopolis.  He randomly drew his other two relics in the first couple turns, and didn't get many Cultists.  Tempest got Localized Hurricane early and was constantly hitting two relics, or a relic and Gloomy, and drawing a ton of cards.  After he flipped, Tempest soon got the Gene-Bound Shackles and it was all over; the Rotting God cost himself 4 HP each turn, and only occasionally got 2 back from eating his own Zombies or a Plummeting Monorail.  Those early Relics actually managed to put the hurt on us really fierce, with Omnitron having had physical Plating at first and thus having to worry about Infernal damage.  This was the first game in which we really experienced any problems from the Grimoire of Curses (the Drum of Despair was still fairly pathetic); having to discard every turn almost from the start of the game was painful, and the fact that all of us would take damage if any of us failed to discard (Omnitron in particular had Components at stake, and Tempest was also bleeding fast) made things feel appropriately, Gloomy-ly miserable, up until we managed to destroy the Grimoire.  It's really a pity that in normal Gloomy games, we seldom even find any of the Relics, let alone all of them; in at least four games against his normal version, he's never flipped, and only the first game was a Relic Victory; the rest of the time, we just kill him (even on advance, with a party specifically chosen to avoid non-physical damage types…I forgot to rule out Mr. Fixer because of Grease Monkey Fist, and that was all it took).

Another first in this game was Tempest's Elemental Subwave Inducer…usually I've found it useless, but in this game, it was really handy after the flip, because infernal damage was happening every turn.  O-X had switched Platings by then, so only Scholar was taking all the pain, and of course that suited him well enough (though I was finally running low on HP by the end).  In one hilarious instance, Gloomy somehow caused Tempest to deal himself damage…and because of the ESI, the damage Tempest dealt was Infernal and was therefore reduced.

He starts with a 25 HP relic you pretty much have to deal with.

Well, unless you have a pair of Focused Plasma Cannons; those made a big difference in getting rid of Skinny.  We did still kill the Pouch of Bones early, but it was a bit less necessary than it might have been.  I debated telling O-X's player that a first-turn Technological Advancement should always fetch Electro-Deployment Unit, but I figured I'd let him learn his own lessons…and as it happened, FPC was perhaps a better choice anyway.

And lord help us if you play Unity or even Visionary against him.

Unity, yes, you're boned there (it kind of neatly balances how much of an edge she has against the likes of La Capitan or Miss Information, that some other villains - Iron Legacy is another one - just brutalize her completely).  For Visionary, having to live without Decoy Projection isn't much of a sacrifice, you can just discard it to Enlighten instead of playing it, no big deal.

(Oddly, Wagner Base with 3 targets may be the best environment choice against him. Are their E-decks with equal or less minions?)

Megalopolis has only one more, but all of them are 10 HP instead of 5, so they're less likely to accidentally die at an inconvenient time, and they're not improving his damage as with Villainous Weaponry.  Indeed, in our game we let Gloomy (and my tanky Scholar) get hit with a train, and that was quite beneficial.  Though of course you never want to let Traffic Jam sit in play unless you're quite certain that the Grimoire is dead and shall remain that way.  ("Klaatu Barada…Necktie!")

Having folks like NightMist (Oblivions are great against him, especially with that nemesis bonus!), Tempest, Expatriette, Fixer, or [redacted] doing global damage help significantly.

Had a game against the Matriarch with a group of newbies. They wanted a challenge after taking out Baron Blade and Grand Warlord Voss, so they insisted on playing a difficulty 4. The team was The Scholar, Tachyon, Unity, and Expatriette. We played against her in the Realm of Discord.

 

So the first turn, the Matriarch played a Carrion Fields. Because of the Mask, she then played Darken the Skies...huh...easiest first turn ever?

 

The rest wasn't much harder. Between The Scholar's tanking and Tachyon's Hypersonic Assaults, any time she got out a bunch of birds, they would get wiped out immediately with no retaliation damage whatsoever. Amusingly, Unity didn't even get a single bot out (due to inexperience and incredibly bad shuffle luck), but it didn't matter. The environment was a non-factor; anything that was threatening was immediately destroyed by Tachyon's Blinding Speed.

 

Huginn and Muninn eventually came out, along with about half her deck in fowls, but by that point Matriarch was down to 17 hit points. Even with the DR 2, The Scholar played Know When to Cut Loose for 8 damage, and Tachyon played Lightspeed Barrage for 11 damage to end the game. We could've claimed we played her on advanced since the cohorts never got destroyed, not that they played much of a factor anyway. The only real damage we took was from two Horrid Cacophonies. The lowest hp on the heroes side was Tachyon with 21 (Positive Energy Field was played), while The Scholar still had all of his hp.

 

So yeah...easiest game against the Matriarch ever?

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Matriarch's games tend to be all-or-nothing; she either destroys you or wimps out completely (whether by drawing the wrong cards or by having all her bird attacks bounce off O-X's Ablative Plating or Scholar's Flesh to Iron).  This is of course completely appropriate; she's a petulant teenage girl with a godlike artifact on her face, so whether she's effective or not largely depends on whether she wakes up on the right side of the bed that afternoon.  Sometimes she'll be executing a power-trip revenge fantasy; other times she'll be goggling over some boy and cook up some ridiculous scheme to try and impress him, only to fail ignominously and end up a sobbing wreck.  She's not exactly supervillain material, personality-wise; she just happens to have some fairly serious mojo, which might work very well if she can actually manage to employ it properly.

The Matriarch isn't normally a lame game, but she is a lame villain, in strictly social-status terms.  The Vengeance Five are all laughing at her behind her back, and she knows it.  But just you wait, she'll show them!  Someday.  Somehow.  She thinks.
